notes: Gold Eagle Deathlands novels 36-70 (1997-2005) plus the 1999 Collector's Edition prequel 'Encounter' (book n=0). Plot sources: Deathlands fandom wiki via its API, archived jamesaxler.com wiki plot pages, worldswithoutend.com blurbs. Rows marked 'our pick' in source.notes are a real place chosen to fit a region the book names only loosely.

sites.name: THE DARK NEON MILE

real.place: Las Vegas Strip (Las Vegas Boulevard South)

sites.shape: regional warlords' blood-sport arena in a dead casino boulevard
sites.notes: arena fights in a resort bowl; tower stubs give sniper lines down the boulevard; car-husk wall closes both ends

source.notes: yearly gathering of rival warlords in the ruins of the casino city, settled by gladiator games

sites.name: THE CANOPY BLOCKS
sites.shape: old-downtown casino blocks under a vaulted canopy, held as a trading floor
sites.notes: a covered street fight; canopy frame is a catwalk; five blocks long so it reads as one corridor

source.notes: the ruined casino city where the arena prisoners and buyers gather; our pick for the old downtown blocks

sites.name: THE FALLEN-WRECK SHORE
sites.shape: mountain lakeshore where a fallen space wreck is hunted
sites.notes: salvage race on a lake between two volcanoes; scattered wreck pieces pull players around the shore loop

source.notes: suspected impact point of a crashed space station that several parties race to strip

sites.name: THE DRY DOCK OF THE DROWNED FLEET
sites.shape: a madman's private navy in an intact submarine base on the marsh coast
sites.notes: set-piece infiltration: wharf, dry dock and bunkers on a marsh grid; fight ends aboard the surfaced hull

source.notes: self-styled admiral rebuilds a naval base around one working nuclear submarine and mines the coast

bunker.notes: real base has hardened missile-handling and weapons storage; the sealed lower level here is plausible only

sites.name: THE OYSTER-SHELL WATERFRONT
sites.shape: quiet river-mouth town trading fish with a naval warlord next door
sites.notes: neutral town on the edge of the base; boats and marsh paths lead to the wharf fight

source.notes: the river-mouth town beside the submarine base; the book places a peaceful sea commune nearby (our pick of the real town)

sites.name: THE SAWGRASS ROAD

real.place: Shark Valley, Tamiami Trail edge of the Everglades

sites.shape: flooded swamp road west of the city where a ruined theme-park bunker lets out
sites.notes: causeway road through open sawgrass; spiral tower is the only height; ambush terrain for boats

source.notes: the crew comes out of a waterlogged bunker in a ruined park just west of the city and heads north; our pick of the real swamp road

sites.name: THE BURIED PHARAOH GATE
sites.shape: god-king city dug out of a buried silent-film Egypt set in coastal dunes
sites.notes: real Hollywood ruin: a 110 ft gate and sphinx avenue buried in dunes, turned into a cult city; dunes shift cover every visit

source.notes: an engineered would-be god enslaves the coast and rebuilds a pyramid city inside an old movie set

sites.name: THE LETTUCE-FIELD CROSSROADS
sites.shape: farm crossroads town on the road to the dune city, paying tribute
sites.notes: calm approach town before the dunes; packing sheds are a good first fight

source.notes: farm town at the edge of the dune field; our pick for the approach to the buried set

sites.name: THE LIBERTY ARCADE

real.place: Freedom Mall site, Freedom Drive (west Charlotte)

sites.shape: enclosed mall run as a trading town with a gladiator ring, besieged by mutants
sites.notes: one-storey mall is a maze of shops; siege defense from the roof; burn-down finale

source.notes: a mall that became a self-run trading town hires the crew as guards against a mutant siege

sites.name: THE TRIANGLE COLD WARD
sites.shape: hospital with a sealed frozen-patient level and a scavenger digging into it
sites.notes: dungeon run: smoke-filled basement to a dead frozen-patient room; the tower is a vertical climb

source.notes: a hospital with a sealed cold-storage level near the bunker; the books name only the city pair (our pick of a campus)

sites.name: THE BLUE-STONE CITY
sites.shape: untouched island city of flat-roof stone streets ruled from a fortress
sites.notes: a rare living city; dense stepped streets; fight moves up to the fort

source.notes: a cheerful, untouched island city whose host scientist hides time experiments in his fortress

sites.name: THE HORNWORK HEADLAND
sites.shape: six-level stone citadel on a headland, a scientist's castle with a teleport room
sites.notes: real 43 m, six-level stone headland fort; climb the levels; machine room hidden in the lowest vault

source.notes: a pleasant host scientist lives in a fortress in the island city and runs a time-machine in its depths

bunker.notes: real fort has vaults and tunnels; the sealed teleport room is plausible only

sites.name: THE PLAGUE-RIVER COUNTY SEAT
sites.shape: mountain hollow town ruled by a healer who fakes a plague to keep people in
sites.notes: narrow river valley: one main street, hills both sides, siege from the ridges; dart-gun enforcers in the woods

source.notes: river-valley town whose healer keeps people trapped by secretly infecting anyone who tries to leave

sites.name: THE GRANITE RIVER RAPIDS

real.place: Pine Flat Dam and Kings River foothills, east of Fresno

sites.shape: Sierra foothill river country where a warrior cult preaches by the gun
sites.notes: river rises in a storm and blocks the ford; the dam crest is the crossing; cult rituals at the tent ground

source.notes: cult of warrior-preachers in the hills near Fresno; the book gives only the area, the dam is our pick

sites.name: THE LAVA-WEIR TOWN

real.place: Idaho Falls (Snake River falls and greenbelt)

sites.shape: river city on a basalt weir, raided by gunmen hunting space debris
sites.notes: falls splits the town; bridges are choke points; elevator is the long sightline

source.notes: the crew is caught near the ruined river city by a warlord's men hunting fallen space-station debris

sites.name: THE BLACK-ROCK RIVER ROAD
sites.shape: river trading post and pirate-haunted water route upriver from the falls
sites.notes: stockade post defended against raiders; boat chase upriver to a pirate-held ship

source.notes: river route with a mother-and-son trading post and river pirates; the book names only the river country

sites.name: THE FOURTEEN-PIER YARD
sites.shape: dead navy yards on the tidewater where a sealed bunker lets out
sites.notes: long piers with hulked ships for cover; open water on three sides

source.notes: the crew arrives in a ruined navy shipyard on the Virginia coast before heading home inland

bunker.notes: the book puts a sealed bunker here; the real base has none known

sites.name: THE TAVERN CROSSROADS
sites.shape: small walled trading crossroads with a tavern where caravans form up
sites.notes: tavern brawl turns firefight; caravan departs at dawn

source.notes: crossroads trading post with a tavern where the crew joins a caravan heading for their home valley

sites.name: THE FORKED-RIVER HOME VALLEY
sites.shape: the hero's home valley town at a river fork, fought over by rival heirs
sites.notes: home turf for the hero; river fork divides the town; real dog-training center fits the town's war-dog trade

source.notes: the hero's home valley, held by his nephew and attacked by old enemies and neighbors

sites.name: THE FOX-HUNT STATION
sites.shape: satellite estate village of a rival valley lord, burned by a sky weapon
sites.notes: small estate village with a castle-style manor; scorched circles from orbit mark the strikes

source.notes: one of the satellite estates around the hero's valley, wrecked by an orbital weapon

sites.name: THE STONE HOUSE CROSSING
sites.shape: satellite estate on an old battlefield creek, ravaged by raiders and a sky weapon
sites.notes: wide-open ridges and a single stone bridge; rolling-field cavalry fights

source.notes: another satellite estate of the valley, mauled by sword-armed raiders and later by the orbital weapon

sites.name: THE PEACH-ORCHARD UPLINK

real.place: Shiloh battlefield and Pittsburg Landing (Tennessee River)

sites.shape: a scientist-warlord's slave-built capital with a satellite uplink on an old battlefield
sites.notes: new-built base on real battlefield ground; bluff landing on the river is the back door; uplink dish is the objective

source.notes: the villain clears the town, enslaves its adults and builds a capital with a satellite uplink controlling an orbital weapon

bunker.notes: the book has a teleport room in this base; real park has none (plausible only)

sites.name: THE QUIET-ZONE DISH

real.place: Green Bank Observatory (National Radio Quiet Zone)

sites.shape: survivor hamlet around a giant listening dish, overrun by a warlord's troops
sites.notes: the 100 m dish dominates an open valley meadow; climb the dish for the best overwatch in the game

source.notes: a small settlement grew around the old radio-telescope dish before being wiped out by the warlord's men

sites.name: THE BENCH-STREET SPRAWL

real.place: Salt Lake City suburbs (Salt Lake Valley benches)

sites.shape: emptied suburb where invaders from another world crossed over
sites.notes: very wide valley grid blocks with the mountain wall above; a dead suburb with one strange scorched park

source.notes: a valley suburb wiped out by scouts from a parallel Earth; later the crew returns to dig up gear buried here

sites.name: THE WALLED TEMPLE BLOCK

real.place: Temple Square and downtown Salt Lake City

sites.shape: downtown blocks turned into a slave-labor mining camp by invaders from another world
sites.notes: real 10-acre block inside a 15 ft wall: a ready-made fortress; jailbreak and sabotage mission

source.notes: invaders from a parallel Earth turn the ruined city into mining grounds worked by slaves in energy shackles

sites.name: THE PEACH-ROW MAIN STREET

real.place: Brigham City (Main Street, foot of the Wellsville Mountains)

sites.shape: mountain-foot farm town struck down by a cholera outbreak
sites.notes: plague town: survivors flee the quarantine; arch over Main Street makes a clean entry shot

source.notes: the crew helps a family escape a valley town struck by cholera

sites.name: THE DRAINED LAKEBED DOOR

real.place: Salt Fork Lake (Salt Fork State Park, Guernsey County)

sites.shape: a sealed bunker opening in a drained reservoir bed, haunted by a robot tank
sites.notes: vehicle-scale map: drive a homemade tank out of the bunker across a drained lakebed while a robot tank hunts you

source.notes: the crew finds a biker-built tank inside a bunker in a drained lakebed and is chased by an old robot tank

bunker.notes: the book's bunker sits in the lakebed; the real park has no bunker (plausible only)

sites.name: THE CROSSED-INTERSTATE TOWN
sites.shape: small city choked by a thinking vine, with a truck stop full of bikers
sites.notes: downtown smothered in vines that drag people into buildings; truck-stop fight on the interchange

source.notes: a vine-choked small city near the bunker, a biker truck stop and a gas station; our pick for the city next to the lake

sites.name: THE GOTHIC CELL CASTLE
sites.shape: a town run from an old state prison by the warden's heirs, with prisoners' heirs as slaves
sites.notes: real castle-gothic prison with 24 ft walls; breakout mission with a three-way revolt finale

source.notes: a town grown inside an old state prison, ruled by the warden's family; the book names no prison, this one is our pick about 70 miles east

sites.name: THE STORM-WRACKED PRAIRIE TOWN
sites.shape: wind-scoured prairie town of outsiders feeding a sealed army bunker
sites.notes: storm-scoured farm town; the crew trains the farmers to assault the bunker

source.notes: oppressed farm people outside a sealed army bunker rise up with the crew's help; the book misplaces the town in Missouri

sites.name: THE BLUFF GARRISON
sites.shape: a fully working army post in a sealed bunker, run by inbred hereditary officers
sites.notes: our pick: the real army post nearest the prairie town; the book's bunker garrison still plays war games for a war already lost

source.notes: a sealed army bunker still run as a working base by inbred soldiers and a bio-computer; the book gives no base, this is our pick

bunker.notes: plausible only; book bunker holds a garrison and a brain-linked computer

sites.name: THE GLASSED LAGOON
sites.shape: a warlord's island kingdom on a nuclear test atoll with PT boats and blast bunkers
sites.notes: flat atoll, thin islands and a huge lagoon: boat combat, bunker raids, reef passes; the books' volcanoes are not real here

source.notes: a tyrant with gunpowder, missiles and working patrol boats rules the old nuclear-test islands

bunker.notes: real atoll has concrete test-instrument bunkers; a deep sealed bunker is plausible only

sites.name: THE BURIED SIDEWALK CITY

real.place: Pioneer Square and the Seattle Underground

sites.shape: an underground town in the buried old streets of a ruined harbor city
sites.notes: two-layer town: ruin above, living streets in the real buried sidewalks below; jungle-hot overgrowth on the surface

source.notes: a gentle underground town beneath the ruined city, whose leader's wife runs secret breeding experiments; later the crew returns near the city

sites.name: THE WAX-MUSEUM HILL

real.place: Clifton Hill and the Skylon Tower, Niagara Falls

sites.shape: a falls-side town of carnival attractions with a lookout tower
sites.notes: falls roar drowns gunfire; tower top scouts the whole farm country; steep hill street to the gorge

source.notes: the crew eats fresh fruit in a falls-side town and scouts a slave-breeding farm from a tower

sites.name: THE MIST-SIDE MILL CITY

real.place: Niagara Falls, New York (downtown and state park)

sites.shape: falls-edge industrial city with an aerospace museum full of old flying machines
sites.notes: cross-river city across the bridge from the attractions; the aircraft museum is the loot target

source.notes: a local guide takes the crew to the old aerospace museum near the falls

sites.name: THE ORCHARD SLAVE FARM

real.place: Niagara Peninsula fruit belt (Lake Ontario shore)

sites.shape: pastoral orchard country run by a tyrant as a slave-breeding farm
sites.notes: rescue mission across orchard rows and vineyards; the escarpment is the high ground

source.notes: pastoral farmland near the falls under a twisted tyrant who breeds slaves; three of the crew are captured

sites.name: THE LIMESTONE LAKEMOUTH FORT

real.place: Old Fort Erie (outlet of Lake Erie)

sites.shape: inbred lakeshore stronghold on the shore of Lake Erie
sites.notes: small two-bastion stone fort at the lake mouth; our pick for the book's lakeshore town

source.notes: an inbred tyrant's town on the shore of Lake Erie buys slaves from the farm; the book gives only the shore, this fort is our pick

sites.name: THE DRY-HOLE BOOMTOWN

real.place: Ranger (1917 oil boom town, Eastland County)

sites.shape: oil-boom town where the tyrant hides that the wells are dry
sites.notes: derrick forest gives vertical cover; sabotage-and-defend missions around the well field

source.notes: a desert tyrant ropes neighbors into a well coalition while secretly faking sabotage; the book names only Texas, this boomtown is our pick

sites.name: THE WHITE PAN PUMPHOUSE

real.place: Salt Flat and the Salt Basin playa (below the Guadalupe Mountains)

sites.shape: adobe town on a vast salt flat ruled by whoever runs the water pumping station
sites.notes: turn the pumps on and the adobe melts: a set-piece where the town dissolves; real white salt pan below a limestone wall

source.notes: a tyrant holds an adobe town on a salt flat by controlling its water pump; when the water runs, the adobe melts

sites.name: THE GYPSUM RANGE POST

real.place: White Sands Missile Range main post (Tularosa Basin)

sites.shape: a sealed desert bunker held by exiles plotting war on two towns
sites.notes: our pick for the book's desert bunker: open desert, blockhouses and a missile park; ambush at a trade meeting

source.notes: a half-mad former guard captain in a desert bunker recruits the crew for his war on two local towns; the book names only the state, this base is our pick

bunker.notes: real range has hardened launch blockhouses; a deep bunker with a teleport room is plausible only

sites.name: THE TABBY-WALL ISLAND

real.place: St. Helena Island (Sea Islands, Beaufort County)

sites.shape: an isolated island community of freedmen's descendants preparing to leave for the mainland
sites.notes: crossing the rip currents is the entry; exodus finale loads the island onto boats

source.notes: the crew is captured by an island people descended from enslaved Africans who are about to move to the mainland; the book names no island (our pick)

sites.name: THE IRRIGATION-GRID CITY
sites.shape: ruined valley city with an old hospital, next to a hunting tyrant's town
sites.notes: grid-street ruin and a hospital raid for the cure; the hunt chases players through these blocks

source.notes: rebels slip a sick crewmate out of the hunting town into the ruined city's hospital

sites.name: THE ORCHARD-RIDGE HUNTING GROUND

real.place: Selah and the Yakima River canyon mouth

sites.shape: small farm town north of the city that sells blood-sport hunts to rich guests
sites.notes: manhunt map: orchard rows, sage ridges and a basalt canyon; guests watch from the stand

source.notes: a farm town that cannot feed itself sells hunts of captured people to visiting rulers; the crew are made the prey

sites.name: THE SUNKEN GREAT PLAZA

real.place: Zocalo and the historic center of Mexico City

sites.shape: half-sunk colonial heart of a huge city, fought over by valley rulers
sites.notes: real square ~240 m across; city sinks into its old lake so the plaza is half flooded; boat-and-rooftop fighting

source.notes: a fair ruler of the drowned capital resists a rival who stages a mutant invasion to unite the valley under him

sites.name: THE QUAKE-PROOF SPIRE
sites.shape: the one tall tower still standing above a drowned city, a scavenger roost
sites.notes: real 166 m tower that rode out the 1985 quake: in the miniature only its top storeys clear the water; vertical sniper nest

source.notes: the crew comes out into the partly sunken ruins of the capital, where only the tallest towers rise above water

sites.name: THE SMOKING MOUNTAIN FLANK
sites.shape: the fuming volcano whose wakening drowned the city, on the valley skyline
sites.notes: skybox landmark and hazard source for the drowned city; a pass over the saddle for raiders from the north

source.notes: the nearby volcanoes, woken by the war, sank the city into its old lakebed

sites.name: THE RIM-HOTEL RAILHEAD
sites.shape: canyon-rim hotel village at a railhead where a war train stops and a caravan is ambushed
sites.notes: everything ends at the rim: a beast is lured over the edge here; the real railway spur ends at the log depot below the hotel

source.notes: a caravan stopped at the canyon edge is hit by raiders; the war train's chase ends at the canyon

sites.name: THE GRAND-HALL VINE STATION

real.place: Kansas City Union Station and Crown Center

sites.shape: vine-choked ruined city where a war train seeks old records in a facility
sites.notes: real 95 ft Grand Hall over a big rail yard; train can roll in; vine spores infect anyone who lingers

source.notes: the general's war train heads into the ruined city for a facility holding records, overgrown with infecting vines

sites.name: THE CLOCK-ARCH TERMINAL
sites.shape: mountain-city rail terminal where a war train refits
sites.notes: warehouse-loft blocks around a granite terminal; the train sits in the yard as a rolling fortress

source.notes: the general's train stops in the mountain city before turning south

sites.name: THE RED-WILLOW TERRACES
sites.shape: multi-storey adobe village on a mountain creek on the war train's southern route
sites.notes: real five-storey adobe stacks on both sides of a creek; ladders and roofs are the fight; the book routes rails through here (no real railroad)

source.notes: the war train detours south through the mountain town on its way to the coast

sites.name: THE SECOND REFINERY TOWN

real.place: El Segundo and its coastal oil refinery

sites.shape: a slave-worked refinery town whose ruler double-crosses a gun-and-fuel convoy
sites.notes: refinery maze; slip in at shift change, plant charges, blow the plant; our pick for the book's coastal refinery town

source.notes: an armored-truck convoy boss wipes out a refinery town in southern California after its ruler double-crosses him; the book names no city, this refinery is our pick

sites.name: THE GULCH TRADING TOWN
sites.shape: frontier trading town where settlers and plains nations meet, besieged by wagon raiders
sites.notes: gulch town with one road in and out; blow the rocks onto the pass to bury the raiders

source.notes: a trading town where whites and plains nations live together beats off wagon-train raiders by bringing down the pass; the book's town is invented, this gulch is our pick

sites.name: THE BEAR LODGE BUTTE

real.place: Devils Tower (Bear Lodge) and the Belle Fourche valley

sites.shape: sacred valley with a cavern of light, fought over by two factions of one nation
sites.notes: our pick for the book's hidden sacred valley: a lone column butte over a river valley; forest-fire set-piece

source.notes: a war chief hires the crew to seize a sacred valley with a healing cavern from a rival faction; the book's valley is invented, this landmark is our pick

sites.name: THE TERRACED COPPER PIT

real.place: Bingham Canyon Mine (Oquirrh Mountains, southwest of Salt Lake City)

sites.shape: giant open-pit mine worked by slaves for invaders from another world
sites.notes: real pit 4 km wide and 1.2 km deep: in miniature a spiral of benches; escape runs up the haul road

source.notes: invaders turn the valley around the ruined city into mining grounds; the book names the city, the copper pit is our pick for the mines

book 57 jumps to a bunker in Utah then marches to the Salt Lake suburbs
book 44 bunker about fifty miles east of Fresno
book 45 has two bunkers, one four days' walk from Idaho Falls, one a tiny gateway armoury in the hills
book 42 bunker near the plague town

the southern California coast broken into quake islands; a boarding school compound in Colorado

a junk fort in the Mojave built by an exiled convoy man (no real anchor)

a cult town about 50 miles from Fresno beside a leaking ruined bunker
a sky-watching scientists' enclave in Montana and their summer dam camp
a caravan road from the coast to the home valley (no specific stops beyond the crossroads)
a toll-taking primitive hamlet near the villain's base
a sunken bunker full of water and dead marines; another bunker wrecked by hunter robots (no locations)
a parallel Earth where the war never happened; a prosperous small town a few hours from the Salt Lake suburbs
a bunker escaping a lava flood (no location); the robot tank and the biker-built tank
an untouched pre-war city guarded by huge winged creatures and a desert town that uses human flesh as fertilizer (no city or state named)
volcanic Pacific islands with an untouched mesa city, a waterfall cliff village and a pirate isle (the real Marshall atolls are flat; geography invented)
a mutant town about 20 miles southwest of the city that worships a painted warhead
a town in a mountain ruin in Nevada (unclear); an inbred river village in Idaho
a women-warrior tribe's march across the northwest (no fixed place)

a mountain town ruled through a mind-controlling fungus in a lake with a pump-house drain; a travelling death-carnival (no region named)

two feuding desert towns in New Mexico (invented); the exiles' bunker (White Sands used as our pick)

a fusion-powered armored war train and its rail bridge over the canyon (no such bridge exists); small furred telepathic creatures near the canyon
the ultimate weapons cache bunker the rivals race for (no location); the refinery town itself (El Segundo used as our pick)
